name: Voyager 2
lastSignal: Still communicating; selected instruments remain active (2026)
tagline: Voyager 2 took the grand tour of the giant planets—and kept travelling after the last close-up worlds fell behind.
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Take advantage of a rare planetary alignment to explore the four giant planets and continue toward interstellar space.
beats.achieved: Voyager 2 flew past Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, returning the only close-up views of Uranus and Neptune obtained by a spacecraft. It crossed the heliopause in 2018.
beats.ending: The mission is ongoing. As its power declines, engineers turn off instruments and nonessential systems in a planned sequence to extend its life.
beats.now: NASA continues to receive data from Voyager 2. Several instruments have been shut down to conserve power, while the spacecraft continues its interstellar mission.
beats.learned: Voyager 2 revealed the diversity of the outer planets and their moons and remains a unique observatory beyond the heliosphere.
